title: Artinian versality at a field-valued point
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ be a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], let $U/S$ be a scheme, and let $x\in\mathcal F(U)$. For a field $K$ [def-weil-field] and a morphism $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], define versality at $\alpha$ by the following lifting property. For every surjection $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of commutative Artinian local rings, every surjection $r:A\twoheadrightarrow K$, every $s':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to S$, every $S$-map $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ for the structural map $\operatorname{Spec}q$ followed by $s'$ such that $a\circ\operatorname{Spec}r=\alpha$, every $\eta\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$, and every specified isomorphism $\eta|_A\cong a^*x$, there exist an $S$-map $b:\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ restricting to $a$ and an isomorphism $\eta\cong b^*x$ restricting to that specified isomorphism. Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means there is a unique maximal ideal. The residue identifications are those induced by $r$ and $rq$; no section of either residue map is assumed.
